assumptions.statement: Labor allocated to accessibility tasks must be recorded in commons_hours telemetry.
Maintenance backlog is degrading one or more systems and must not be obscured by mobility tasks.

expected_effects.rationale: Explicit tracking of accessibility labor may reveal previously hidden burden.
Proper labor allocation may unblock review domains faster than hiding labor.

hypothesis: Labor required for accessibility verification must be tracked against maintenance_hours to prevent untracked resident work.

queries: CIaC mobility access warning interventions expected effects labor energy privacy public health governance accessibility scenario resilience

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Use metrics_to_compare to ensure resource_telemetry.resources.current_ratio remains stable.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Visibility of labor burden may reduce apparent efficiency metrics

risk_tradeoffs.mitigation: Ensure consent and privacy governance assumptions remain explicit.
risk_tradeoffs.risk: Privacy risks if resident location data used for surveys

acceptance_tests: No new survival-critical unmet demand is introduced.
No labor is shifted into untracked resident burden.
Privacy, consent, public-health, accessibility, and governance assumptions remain explicit.

title: Resident survey labor allocation protocol
